assessments.technical_explanation: The supplied source is minified code matching the public Preact virtual-DOM library bundled with the HTM tagged-template parser, exported under the standard rendering and hook names that a build-step-free browser extension would use. Its data flow is entirely DOM-local: vnode construction, diffing, element creation and insertion, attribute and event-listener management, and hook state tracking. The only link-like literal in the file is the W3C SVG namespace string passed to namespace-aware element creation; it is an identifier, never fetched or navigated to. There is no fetch, XHR, WebSocket, dynamic import, script or iframe injection, credential access, or any other outbound data flow in the supplied text. The scanner's link heuristic almost certainly matched that namespace constant; a fixed scanner signal of medium severity without a demonstrated network destination or untrusted-input path is not demonstrated exposure.
assessments.layman_explanation: This file is a compressed copy of a widely used free library that draws on-screen interfaces, which the extension bundles so it can work without build tools. The automated scanner thought it saw a suspicious web address, but the only address present is a fixed label that browsers require when creating vector graphics elements; nothing is ever contacted over the network. The file contains no code for sending or receiving data anywhere, hiding activity, or touching your information.

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged literal is a loopback address on the standard ComfyUI port, used only as the default value for a user-configurable image-generation server setting. Actual network behavior falls into two categories: generation requests go to SillyTavern's own same-origin proxy endpoints, and one direct multipart upload of the user's own prepared portrait PNG is sent to the user-configured ComfyUI instance (with an opaque no-CORS retry when headers are absent) because the host has no upload route. Both destinations are chosen by the user in the extension's image settings, match the project's documented ComfyUI image-generation feature, carry only prompts and locally generated image data, and involve no credentials. This is proportionate, disclosed, and expected for the stated purpose; the plain-HTTP link warning is a scanner heuristic flagging the local default URL, not evidence of a suspicious external destination.
assessments.layman_explanation: The flagged web address is just the standard local address where ComfyUI (a popular image-generation program) runs on your own computer. The extension uses it as a starting suggestion for a setting you control, sends your image prompts through SillyTavern itself, and uploads a picture to your own ComfyUI so it can paint expressions from it. Nothing goes to any external or unexpected place, and no passwords or keys are involved.

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged line constructs DOM elements in a vendored Preact/htm rendering library and uses the standard W3C SVG namespace identifier as the argument to the namespace-aware element creation call. That identifier is an opaque name required by the DOM API to create SVG elements; it is never fetched, resolved, or contacted over the network. The supplied module is a conventional virtual-DOM renderer with hooks and a tagged-template markup parser, containing no network requests, no dynamic code evaluation, and no outbound data flow. The scanner's URL-adjacent heuristic matched a namespace constant, not a network destination.
assessments.layman_explanation: The scanner saw a web-address-shaped string inside a bundled interface-building library. That string is simply the official label browsers require when drawing SVG graphics; using it never opens an internet connection or sends anything anywhere. This is a false alarm on ordinary, widely used library code.

assessments.technical_explanation: The two flagged literals are loopback addresses on the well-known default ports for LM Studio and Ollama, listed as convenient defaults for local OpenAI-compatible inference providers. All substantive operations route through SillyTavern's own same-origin endpoints: API keys are written to and rotated in the host's secret store, model lists are fetched via the host's status proxy, and connection profiles store only a secret identifier, never the key value. The only other URLs present are the official vendor console pages for obtaining keys, displayed to the user as links. There is no direct outbound connection to any of these addresses from this module, no key material leaves the host's secret store, and the design deliberately avoids placing secrets in extension settings. This matches the project's stated provider-setup purpose and represents a above-baseline handling practice for credentials.
assessments.layman_explanation: The flagged addresses are just the standard local addresses where LM Studio and Ollama run on your own computer; they are offered as defaults for connecting to those programs. Any API keys you enter are saved into SillyTavern's own secure key storage, never into the extension's settings or sent anywhere by this code, and model lists are fetched through SillyTavern itself. This is exactly what a provider setup screen is supposed to do.
